market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate: Banks Face Tight Deadlines
market.summary_short: The EU's Instant Payments Regulation mandates banks to offer instant credit transfers at no extra cost, with strict deadlines for implementation. This will significantly accelerate payment processing across the Eurozone.
market.summary_detail: The European Union's Instant Payments Regulation, officially adopted, requires all payment service providers (PSPs) in the Eurozone to offer instant credit transfers within 10 seconds, 24/7, 365 days a year. A key provision is that charges for instant payments must not exceed those for traditional SEPA credit transfers. Banks in the Eurozone must be ready to receive instant payments by early 2027 and send them by mid-2027. Non-Eurozone EU member states have a longer transition period. The regulation also includes a Verification of Payee (VoP) requirement to combat fraud, which banks must implement. This represents a major shift in European payment infrastructure, pushing for real-time liquidity and improved cash management for corporates.
key_points: Mandatory instant credit transfers within 10 seconds.
No additional fees compared to standard SEPA credit transfers.
Eurozone banks: Receive by early 2027, send by mid-2027.
Includes mandatory Verification of Payee (VoP) for fraud prevention.
market.rbi_cash_management: This regulation is critical for CMIplus. RBI must ensure all network banks in Eurozone CEE countries (e.g., Slovakia, Austria) are fully compliant by the deadlines. CMIplus needs to support instant payment initiation and receipt, integrate VoP functionality, and ensure competitive pricing. This enhances RBI's real-time cash management offering for international corporates.

market.title: SWIFT CBPR+ Migration: Corporates Must Accelerate Adoption
market.summary_short: The global migration to ISO 20022 for cross-border payments via SWIFT CBPR+ is progressing, with banks and corporates facing deadlines for full adoption. This standardisation promises richer data and improved reconciliation.
market.summary_detail: The SWIFT CBPR+ program, mandating the use of ISO 20022 for cross-border payments, is moving towards its final stages. While banks have been actively migrating, corporates are now urged to accelerate their adoption to leverage the benefits of richer, structured payment data. The co-existence period, where both MT and MX formats are supported, is set to end, making full ISO 20022 compliance essential for seamless international transactions. This transition impacts treasury systems, ERP integrations, and payment factories, requiring significant IT and process adjustments. The enhanced data capabilities of ISO 20022 are expected to improve reconciliation, reduce manual errors, and facilitate better liquidity management for multinational corporations.
key_points: SWIFT CBPR+ mandates ISO 20022 for cross-border payments.
Co-existence period for MT and MX formats is ending.
Corporates need to update ERP/TMS for richer data.
Promises improved reconciliation and liquidity management.
market.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus must fully support ISO 20022 MX messages for all cross-border and multi-currency payments, both inbound and outbound. This includes ensuring proper data mapping, validation, and enrichment capabilities within the platform and its H2H/EBICS/SWIFT channels. RBI needs to guide CEE corporates through this transition, highlighting the benefits for their treasury operations and ensuring seamless connectivity with their ERP/TMS systems.

market.title: PSD3 Proposals Emerge: New Era for Open Banking
market.summary_short: The European Commission's proposals for PSD3 and the new Financial Data Access (FIDA) framework aim to strengthen Open Banking, enhance consumer protection, and expand data sharing beyond payments. This will reshape the financial services landscape.
market.summary_detail: The European Commission has released its proposals for PSD3 (Payment Services Directive 3) and a new regulation on Financial Data Access (FIDA), signaling a significant evolution for Open Banking. PSD3 aims to improve payment security, combat fraud, and ensure fair competition, building on the foundations of PSD2. FIDA, on the other hand, seeks to enable customers to share their financial data (beyond payment accounts) with third-party providers, fostering innovation across a broader range of financial services. These regulations will likely lead to new API standards, increased data portability, and potentially new business models for banks and FinTechs. Corporates could benefit from more integrated financial services and advanced cash management tools, but also face new data privacy and security considerations.
key_points: PSD3 aims to enhance payment security and fraud prevention.
FIDA expands data sharing beyond payment accounts to broader financial data.
New API standards and increased data portability expected.
Impacts bank-FinTech collaboration and corporate financial services.
market.rbi_cash_management: The evolution of Open Banking under PSD3/FIDA is crucial for CMIplus's API strategy. RBI needs to monitor these developments closely to adapt its Open API offerings, potentially expanding beyond payment initiation and account information to broader financial data services. This could enable CMIplus to offer more sophisticated liquidity management, treasury reporting, and integrated ERP solutions, while also strengthening fraud prevention measures like VoP.

market.title: EU Instant Payments Regulation Drives ISO 20022 Adoption
market.summary_short: New EU regulation mandates instant payments, accelerating ISO 20022 migration across Europe. Banks and corporates face tight deadlines to comply with real-time processing requirements.
market.summary_detail: The recent EU Instant Payments Regulation, effective from early 2025 for receiving and early 2026 for sending, is a game-changer for European treasury. It requires all EU banks to offer instant credit transfers in EUR, free of charge, within 10 seconds, 24/7/365. This mandate significantly accelerates the full migration to ISO 20022 for all payment types, as the richer data standard is crucial for efficient real-time processing, reconciliation, and fraud detection. Corporates must prepare their ERP and TMS systems to handle the new messaging format and the increased speed of transactions, impacting liquidity management and cash forecasting. The regulation also includes provisions for sanctions screening, adding another layer of complexity.

Effective early 2025 (receiving) and early 2026 (sending).
Accelerates full ISO 20022 migration for all payment types.
Impacts corporate liquidity, reconciliation, and fraud screening.

market.title: Open Banking APIs Transform Corporate Treasury Operations
market.summary_short: Corporate treasurers are increasingly leveraging Open Banking APIs for real-time data access and automated processes. This shift enhances visibility and control over global cash positions.
market.summary_detail: The adoption of Open Banking APIs is moving beyond retail banking into the corporate treasury space, driven by the need for greater efficiency and real-time insights. Treasurers are using APIs to connect directly with bank accounts, retrieve real-time balance and transaction data, initiate payments, and automate reconciliation processes. This direct connectivity bypasses traditional file-based transfers, offering immediate access to financial information across multiple banks and regions. The trend is fostering a more integrated treasury ecosystem, enabling advanced cash forecasting, automated liquidity management, and improved working capital optimization. Security and standardization remain key considerations for widespread adoption.

Enables automation of payments and reconciliation.
Enhances multi-bank cash visibility and forecasting.
Security and standardization are critical for corporate adoption.

market.title: AI-Powered Fraud Prevention Critical for Real-Time Payments
market.summary_short: The rise of instant payments intensifies the need for advanced, AI-powered fraud detection systems. Corporates and banks must collaborate to combat sophisticated cyber threats.
market.summary_detail: With instant payments becoming the norm, the window for detecting and preventing fraudulent transactions has shrunk dramatically, often to mere seconds. This necessitates a paradigm shift in fraud prevention strategies, moving towards real-time, predictive analytics powered by Artificial Intelligence and machine learning. These systems can analyze vast amounts of transaction data, identify unusual patterns, and flag suspicious activities before payments are irrevocably settled. Business Email Compromise (BEC) and invoice fraud remain significant threats, with fraudsters adapting quickly to new payment rails. Enhanced collaboration between corporates, banks, and technology providers is essential to share threat intelligence and implement robust multi-layered security protocols, including Verification of Payee (VoP) solutions.
key_points: Instant payments reduce fraud detection window to seconds.
AI/ML is crucial for real-time, predictive fraud prevention.
BEC and invoice fraud remain prevalent threats.
Collaboration and VoP solutions are vital for robust security.
market.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus must prioritize integrating advanced fraud prevention tools, including AI-driven analytics and VoP, into its platform. RBI should educate clients on best practices for cyber security and offer solutions that mitigate risks associated with real-time payments across CEE.

market.title: ISO 20022 Migration: SWIFT MT-MX Coexistence Challenges Persist
market.summary_short: The global migration to ISO 20022 for cross-border payments continues, with financial institutions navigating the complexities of the MT-MX coexistence period. Data enrichment and interoperability remain key challenges for corporate treasuries.
market.summary_detail: The SWIFT CBPR+ migration to ISO 20022 is a multi-year initiative to standardize payment messaging globally, enhancing data richness and automation. While the initial 'go-live' for many regions was in March 2023, the coexistence period, where both MT and MX formats are supported, extends until November 2025. This period presents significant challenges for banks and corporates in ensuring accurate data translation, maintaining interoperability between old and new systems, and fully leveraging the richer data capabilities of ISO 20022 for reconciliation and fraud detection. Many CEE banks are still in various stages of their internal system upgrades, impacting how quickly corporates can fully benefit from the new standard's potential.

market.title: EU/UK Banks Face One-Year T+1 Settlement Deadline
market.summary_short: EU and UK banks are under pressure to prepare for the upcoming move to next-day settlement (T+1), with only one year remaining until the deadline. This shift will significantly impact operational readiness for financial institutions and their corporate clients.
market.summary_detail: Financial institutions in both the European Union and the United Kingdom are facing a critical one-year countdown to demonstrate their operational readiness for the transition to T+1 settlement. This regulatory change mandates that securities transactions settle one business day after the trade date, a significant acceleration from the current T+2 standard. The move aims to reduce market risk, improve capital efficiency, and align with global trends, particularly the US market's earlier adoption of T+1. Banks must ensure their back-office systems, reconciliation processes, and liquidity management capabilities are robust enough to handle the compressed settlement cycle. This will require substantial investment in technology and process re-engineering to avoid potential penalties and maintain competitive advantage.

regulatory.title: EU Instant Payments Regulation Mandates Universal SEPA Real-Time Processing
regulatory.summary_short: The new EU regulation requires all payment service providers to offer instant payments in euro, ensuring funds are credited within ten seconds. This aims to make instant payments universally available and affordable across the EU.
regulatory.summary_detail: The EU Instant Payments Regulation (EU) 2024/886, which entered into force recently, mandates that all EU payment service providers (PSPs) offering SEPA credit transfers must also offer instant credit transfers in euro. Key provisions include ensuring funds are credited to the payee's account within ten seconds, regardless of the day or time, and that charges for instant payments cannot exceed those for traditional SEPA credit transfers. PSPs must also implement a mandatory verification of payee (VoP) service to prevent fraud. The regulation aims to boost the adoption of instant payments, fostering innovation and competition in the retail payments market across the EU and EEA.
key_points: Mandatory offering of instant payments for all euro PSPs.
Funds credited within 10 seconds, 24/7/365.
Pricing capped at standard SEPA credit transfer fees.

regulatory.summary_detail: The Eurosystem's TARGET2 (T2) system, a key component of TARGET Services, completed its migration to the ISO 20022 messaging standard as part of the T2-T2S consolidation project. regulatory.title: EBA Fraud Taxonomy 7.0 Released, Effective January 2027
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA has updated its Fraud Taxonomy to version 7.0, effective January 1, 2027, to reflect the latest fraud trends and support harmonised pan-European fraud-fighting. This taxonomy provides a standardised framework for classifying payment fraud, aiding compliance with forthcoming Payment Services Regulation.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) released version 7.0 of its Fraud Taxonomy on June 3, 2026, with an effective date of January 1, 2027. This update incorporates the latest fraud trends identified by the Expert Group on Payment Fraud-related Topics (EGPF). Key changes include replacing 'emotional manipulation' with more specific modi like 'support a friend or family member fraud', 'romance fraud', and 'charity / donation fraud', and adding new labels for suspected money mule activity and 'card chip relay' fraud. The taxonomy provides a harmonised pan-European vocabulary and categorisation approach for all payment fraud types, including card transactions. It is designed to improve fraud monitoring, reporting, and information sharing, explicitly supporting data classification for information-sharing arrangements under the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSD3/PSR).
key_points: EBA Fraud Taxonomy version 7.0 released on June 3, 2026.
Effective date for implementation is January 1, 2027.

regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI/CMIplus must ensure internal fraud monitoring, reporting, and classification systems are updated to align with EBA Fraud Taxonomy v7.0 by January 1, 2027. regulatory.summary_short: The EBA's Open Finance Working Group published a report on 'Supercharging embedded finance with agentic AI,' identifying key use cases and future roles for financial institutions. This report provides strategic guidance for banks navigating the evolving Open Finance landscape, which is closely linked to upcoming regulations like FIDA.
regulatory.summary_detail: On June 10, 2026, the Euro Banking Association (EBA) released a new report by its Open Finance Working Group (OFWG) titled 'Supercharging embedded finance with agentic AI.' The report aims to identify specific use cases within embedded finance where leveraging agentic AI could significantly benefit financial institutions. It also delineates future roles for banks in this evolving ecosystem. This publication is crucial for understanding the strategic direction of Open Finance, which is expected to be shaped by the forthcoming Financial Data Access (FIDA) regulation. While not a direct regulatory mandate, the report provides insights into best practices and potential operational shifts for financial institutions in the context of advanced Open Banking and AI integration.
key_points: Report 'Supercharging embedded finance with agentic AI' published on June 10, 2026.
Identifies use cases for agentic AI in embedded finance for financial institutions.
Delineates future roles for banks in the evolving Open Finance ecosystem.
Provides strategic guidance relevant to upcoming Open Banking/FIDA regulations.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI/CMIplus should review this report to understand the strategic implications of agentic AI and embedded finance for its corporate cash management platform. This includes assessing potential for new API-driven services, enhanced data analytics, and operational efficiencies, aligning with the future direction of Open Banking and FIDA for CEE clients.
